issues.legal_issue: Expenditure incurred to provide facilities owned by a municipality in exchange for immunity from municipal charges is revenue expenditure deductible from business profits when it creates no capital asset or change in the taxpayer’s capital structure.
material_facts: The taxpayer operated a cement factory and incurred expenditure under an agreement to construct water-supply pipelines and related facilities for a town.
The municipality took ownership of the facilities outside the taxpayer’s premises and was responsible for their future maintenance.
In exchange for providing amenities and services, the taxpayer obtained immunity under normal conditions from municipal rates, taxes and charges.
The expenditure was incurred for the taxpayer’s business, and the dispute concerned whether it was capital or revenue expenditure.
The expenditure created no capital asset for the taxpayer and did not change its capital structure.
issues.conclusion: The expenditure was revenue expenditure and was deductible from the taxpayer’s profits; the appeal challenging the deduction was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(2)(xv) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the classification of expenditure depends on the commercial nature of the advantage and whether it lies in the capital field. The enduring-benefit test stated in Atherton v. British Insulated and Helsby Cables Ltd. and approved in Assam Bengal Cement Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax is not conclusive; as explained in Empire Jute Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, an enduring advantage may still be revenue in nature if it facilitates business while leaving fixed capital untouched. An advantage that substitutes for liabilities that would themselves be revenue outgoings is in the revenue field, particularly where no asset accrues to the taxpayer.

rule.if: tax_deduction_appeal and business_purpose and municipal_ownership_of_facilities and immunity_from_revenue_charges and no_taxpayer_capital_asset and no_change_in_capital_structure

predicates.tax_deduction_appeal: The proceeding concerns whether business expenditure is deductible in determining taxable profits.
predicates.business_purpose: The taxpayer incurred the expenditure for the purposes of its business.
predicates.municipal_ownership_of_facilities: The facilities produced by the expenditure were owned and maintained by the municipality rather than by the taxpayer.
predicates.immunity_from_revenue_charges: The taxpayer obtained immunity from charges that, if paid, would have been revenue expenses.
predicates.no_taxpayer_capital_asset: The expenditure did not create a capital asset belonging to the taxpayer.
predicates.no_change_in_capital_structure: The expenditure did not alter or add to the taxpayer’s capital structure.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer’s business expenditure creates municipality-owned facilities, secures immunity from revenue charges, and adds nothing to the taxpayer’s capital assets or structure, the expenditure is deductible as revenue expenditure.
